fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time conspicuity of a HAWK display is a substantive safety issue at final design: driver misread or late detection of the stop indication directly threatens pedestrians crossing the arterial, and remediation is still feasible at this stage.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim (drivers confused by competing background visual elements at night at Speedway Blvd/Rook Ave) rests on a verbatim quoted site-specific observation in EV-US-001 traced to the FHWA case study Issue 6, exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety concern under FHWA RSA practice with no compliance/MUTCD question conflated into it, and conspicuity treatment remains within final-design-stage scope.
justifications.recommendation_quality: A reflective border around the HAWK signal head is a specific, actionable, low-cost and viable countermeasure directly targeting the identified night-time background-confusion problem.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed road users should drivers misread or detect the display late, tying driver conspicuity to VRU protection as required.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance timing at HAWK/PHB crossings on the corridor's highest pedestrian collision sites is a real, scheme-relevant safety issue for slower walkers, not vacuous.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim (clearance may be short for elderly pedestrians) is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US-016, with the recorded case-study TABLE A.10 Issue 2 anchoring these exact sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern rather than a compliance claim; verifying assumed walking speeds behind signal timing respects FHWA/HAWK framework semantics without conflating MUTCD compliance.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: reprogramme clearance intervals at all six named sites using a reduced assumed walking speed, which is feasible at final design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Vulnerable road users are central—pedestrians and elderly pedestrians are named road users and the entire finding addresses their crossing exposure.
